I build the thing to understand it.

I am Deshna Sharma, a Grade 12 student at Jayshree Periwal International School. For two years I have built eyewear that blocks only the headlight glare and lets the rest of the road stay visible. It is patented, published and prize-winning, and it is still not finished.

Main project · January 2024 to today

Selective Dynamic Glare-Blocking Eyewear

Glasses that darken only the patch of the lens where a headlight is, and follow it. Tinted and polarised lenses dim the whole view. On a dark road that makes driving less safe, not more. My hand, held up against the glare, already showed that only one spot needs blocking. I built a small version of the hand.

1

The problem, measured

Walking home one night a car's high beam blinded me for a few seconds and left me with a headache. I went round my housing society with a list of questions. Everyone who goes out at night had the problem, in a car, on a scooter or on a bicycle. The Times of India reported that high-beam glare was blamed for 1,470 accidents in one Indian city in one year.

2

Five ideas, four rejected

A mechanical hand on the windscreen was flimsy and worked only in a car. A tint that drops in front of the eyes still blocked the whole view. The idea that survived: a lens that darkens one spot and moves it with the light.

▶ 5:31Ideas?video 2 ▶ 2:35Smart shades?video 3
3

Learning displays by taking them apart

I did not know how a transparent display could work, so I stripped an LCD down to its layers, pulled the polariser sheets off, and drove a bare chip-on-glass LCD from an Arduino on a breadboard. That became the lens.

▶ 5:08display technologiesvideo 4 the transparent lensat 3:45
4

Code that finds the glare

A camera takes a frame. My Python code (OpenCV) keeps the pixels above a brightness threshold, finds the centre of the brightest cluster, and draws a solid black circle there on two LCDs, one per eye. The wearer sizes the circle to the glare. The first version ran on a Raspberry Pi; the Arduino side is C++.

the flowchartcode video threshold maskcode video
5

Three prototypes, tested on people

Prototype 1: a stripped 7-inch display on a Raspberry Pi with a fixed mask. Prototype 2: a static black circle on a chip-on-glass LCD, so 15 to 20 testers could hide a torch behind it and read text on a whiteboard through the lens. They reported about half the glare gone and could still read. Prototype 3: camera, two lenses, a 3D-printed frame I designed, and the moving mask.

Some testers said existing glasses were good enough, so I compared my lens with tinted and polarised lenses by image analysis: median intensity, contrast and edge energy, in the glare, the transition and the background. Mine kept the most background detail with the smoothest transition.

6

Patent, paper, First Place

I searched existing patents, then filed Indian patent application 202411053278, published 9 August 2024. My father and I wrote it up as a conference paper for the 5th IEOM India International Conference at VIT Vellore in November 2025, where it won First Place in the High School STEM Competition. He is co-inventor and co-author: he advised me and provided resources from his office and factory. I developed the code, assembled the prototypes and ran the testing.

What is still wrong with it: too slow, too bulky, and the tracking lags when the glare moves. That is the work I want to do next, with proper signal processing, embedded computing and optics.

Industry · May 2026

Four days inside a motorcycle company

Hero MotoCorp Young Innovators ProgramJaipur cohort · 18 to 23 May 2026

Selected from more than 800 applicants nationwide. A team of five under an Innovation Manager, four days to design and pitch a delivery box for food-delivery riders and emergency medical supplies: two temperature-controlled zones, a quick-release mount, a PIN lock, a temperature display and a suspension.

I asked the mentor to let me run most of it. He told me to trust the team. So I built the CAD model with every function the team proposed and designed the final pitch as a mind map, while each teammate owned one function. We presented to the company's senior managers at the close. I also watched a large manufacturer move from sketch to clay model to tested product, which is how I now think about my own eyewear: a product, not a demo.

Physics by building

If I can make it happen on the bench, I believe it

Physics Internal AssessmentIB · tyre pressure vs rolling resistance

Cycling to school at low tyre pressure made me push harder, so I measured it. I built three laser and LDR break-beam gates and an Arduino that logs the timings in C++. Two speeds over a known distance give the deceleration. My fitted exponent was −0.463 ± 0.132 against the published −0.477.

Extended EssayIB · photoelasticity

Stress around a hole in a polycarbonate beam under three-point bending. I derived the stress concentration factor for bending myself, built a circular polariscope, tested 15 beams across five hole sizes and three loads, and wrote fringe-counting code to read the results.

DemonstrationsGrade 10 onwards

I did not want to memorise Fleming's rules, so I hung a wire between magnets and reversed the current to watch it jump the other way. I filmed it for my class. The same habit produced videos on transformers, LCD polarisers and induced emf, and IGCSE notes that helped a classmate reach an A* in French.
